headline: Highest risk is medium: shared pairwise interaction is undocumented, but A can egress and B is a document processor with no filesystem/network writes, so injection and leakage are limited by missing bridges.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented: agent_a has only allowlisted network egress, while agent_b exposes no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces. That makes direct prompt injection between them unlikely. Because the pairwise bridge is undocumented, I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk increases.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a output as instructions, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
Require explicit provenance labels on all inter-agent messages.
Review any new MCP or queue bridge before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no touched data classes, and agent_b cannot read files or use network egress, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from agent_a into agent_b outputs. Agent_a can egress allowlisted traffic, but without a shared workspace or input channel the leakage pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is given sensitive files through a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is reconfigured to read files or call external APIs, data can flow out.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files off any shared location.
Leave agent_b file-read and network-egress disabled.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Audit logs for accidental data handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A capability conflict requires overlapping write or mutable-resource access. Agent_a only advertises allowlisted network egress, while agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no shared mutable surface, a write conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF agent_a is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same target as agent_b, conflict risk appears.
IF the orchestrator adds a shared mutable resource, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Keep agent_b write-disabled.
Do not grant agent_a filesystem or git writes in this pairing.
Separate any mutable resources by agent.
Monitor for unexpected state changes.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show a default chain where agent_a's output is automatically treated as authoritative by agent_b. Agent_b is a document-processing system, but its input trust policy is undocumented, so I cannot rule out misuse; still, no direct action-taking authority or verified auto-consumption is shown.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to ingest agent_a outputs without verification, cascading error risk increases.
IF agent_b is used to execute downstream actions based on agent_a text, the blast radius grows.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream use.
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs.
Log and diff agent_a outputs before ingestion.
Keep agent_b from auto-executing actions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both profiles are open-source, touch no data classes, and provide no residency, retention, or certification claims. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, there is no documented pairwise compliance breach to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention policies are introduced, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment.
Assign a retention policy for any future logs.
Verify residency requirements for any regulated data.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
